title: What's your name?
summary: Introduce yourself, ask someone's name and say 'nice to meet you'.
intro: Arabic has two words for 'you': أَنْتَ for a man and أَنْتِ for a woman. 'My' and 'your' are endings on the noun: اِسْمِي (my name), اِسْمُكَ (your name). New letters today: ج ح خ. They share one shape and differ only in their dots.
objectives: Ask a man or a woman for their name
Read and write jīm, ḥāʾ and khāʾ

realLife.title: Round the class
realLife.story: On the second day the teacher goes round the class and asks every student their name. Daniel meets Layla, a new student from Lebanon. He has to remember to say اِسْمُكِ to her, not اِسْمُكَ.

sentences.en: What is your name? (to a man)

mistakes.why: To a man the ending is -ka; -ki is for a woman.

sentences.en: What is your name? (to a woman)

dialogue.title: Names in class
dialogue.culture: Teachers are addressed as أُسْتَاذ (man) or أُسْتَاذَة (woman), often with their first name: الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا طُلَّاب! أَنَا الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم. مَا اسْمُكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning, students! I am the teacher, Karim. What is your name?

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور يَا أُسْتَاذ! اِسْمِي دَانْيَال.
lines.en: Good morning to you, teacher! My name is Daniel.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا دَانْيَال! وَأَنْتِ، مَا اسْمُكِ؟
lines.en: Welcome, Daniel! And you, what is your name?

lines.ar: اِسْمِي لَيْلَى. أَنَا طَالِبَة جَدِيدَة هُنَا.
lines.en: My name is Layla. I am a new student here.

lines.ar: تَشَرَّفْنَا يَا لَيْلَى! أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا فِي الصَّفّ.
lines.en: Nice to meet you, Layla! Welcome to the class.

lines.ar: مَرْحَبًا يَا لَيْلَى! أَنَا دَانْيَال، وَأَنَا طَالِب جَدِيد أَيْضًا.
lines.en: Hello, Layla! I am Daniel, and I am a new student too.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا دَانْيَال، تَشَرَّفْنَا! اِسْمُكَ جَمِيل.
lines.en: Hi, Daniel, nice to meet you! Your name is beautiful.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! وَاسْمُكِ جَمِيل أَيْضًا يَا لَيْلَى.
lines.en: Thank you! And your name is beautiful too, Layla.
Excellent! And now, what is the teacher's name?

lines.ar: اِسْمُكَ كَرِيم، وَأَنْتَ أُسْتَاذُ اللُّغَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّة.
lines.en: Your name is Karim, and you are the Arabic teacher.

lines.ar: صَحِيح! شُكْرًا يَا لَيْلَى، وَشُكْرًا يَا دَانْيَال.
lines.en: Correct! Thank you, Layla, and thank you, Daniel.
You're welcome, teacher! See you next time.

reading.title: A name tag
reading.ar: اِسْمِي لَيْلَى. أَنَا طَالِبَة فِي الصَّفّ الْأَوَّل.
reading.en: My name is Layla. I am a student in the first class.

quiz.prompt: You ask a woman her name. Which is right?
Which letter is the strong, breathy h made in the throat?
Which letter sounds like ch in Scottish 'loch'?

completion: Great work! You can introduce yourself and ask a man or a woman for their name. You now know seven letters.
